title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 290 (Powers and duties of company liquidator)

content.overview: The company liquidator may, with the sanction of the Tribunal where the section requires it, carry on the business, institute or defend suits, sell property, raise money, and do the other acts the section lists.
content.glance: The company liquidator may, with the sanction of the Tribunal where the section requires it, carry on the business, institute or defend suits, sell property, raise money, and do the other acts the section lists.
content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 290 (Powers and duties of company liquidator). The company liquidator may, with the sanction of the Tribunal where the section requires it, carry on the business, institute or defend suits, sell property, raise money, and do the other acts the section lists. Apply only the conditions, approvals, filings and penalties stated in the section. A rule made under the Act cannot contradict the section. Not a verified closure.

sections.heading: Explanation
sections.body: Some powers need sanction; others may be exercised subject to the Tribunal's control. The liquidator acts for the benefit of the liquidation, not as a continuing board.
